newsitem.title: POLAND: Sliding dollar, brewery deal push zloty higher.
newsitem.headline: Sliding dollar, brewery deal push zloty higher.

text.p: The half pfennig slide of the U.S. dollar coupled with a payment of a $75 million privatisation deal of the Poland's Tyskie brewery pushed the zloty upward against the basket of currencies on Tuesday, dealers said.

They said most of the privatisation deal, sheduled to go through the market this week, may have been placed at the post-trade fixing with the central bank, but that banks sold currencies in anticipation of the transaction.
"Payment for the Tyskie brewer had a large psychological impact on the market today, even if a part or even all of the deal was done at the fixing," said Przemyslaw Ciszecki of ING.
Earlier in October a company formed by South African Breweries Ltd (SAB) and Poland's Euro Agro Centrum SA bought a 52 percent stake in the Tychy brewery for $75 million.
On Tuesday the zloty closed at 2.03/1.99 percent below the trading band centre, stronger than Monday's 1.96/1.90.
It was at 2.8070/80 to the dollar, up from 2.8125/30 on Monday and at 1.8397/07 to the mark, down from 1.8375/90.

One-day deposit rates inched down on Tuesday as more banks found excess cash to place, braking the virtual strangle-hold the few lenders had on short-term deposit rates during the first week of October, dealers said.

"Only a few banks had cash early in the month and they kept rates artificially high because they knew others had to finance daily needs and that there would be takers," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.
Overnight rates closed at 19.0/19.50 percent, down a point from Monday's close at 20.0/20.5 percent, and tomorrow/next rates were at 19.0/19.5 percent, also down from 20.45/20.55.
Investors bid for 245 million zlotys worth of bids at today's 700 million zloty 10-year floating bond auction.
